title: Trust Boundaries and Untrusted Input
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of trust boundaries and untrusted input.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: A trust boundary is where data or control crosses between components with different levels of trust—for example, a browser and a server, a user and an application, or one service and another. Data received across a boundary should be considered untrusted until checked for the context and rules that apply. Client-side checks improve usability but cannot replace server-side validation.
understand.whyItMatters: Boundaries help developers identify where validation, authorization, and safe handling must occur.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
A trust boundary is where data or control crosses between components with different levels of trust—for example, a browser and a server, a user and an application, or one service and another. Data received across a boundary should be considered untrusted until checked for the context and rules that apply. Client-side checks improve usability but cannot replace server-side validation.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.title: Identify a boundary
examples.explanation: A browser-to-server transition is a trust boundary.

examples.title: Mark data as untrusted
examples.explanation: Treat external values as data, not as instructions.

examples.title: Do not rely only on UI checks
examples.explanation: A server must independently enforce important rules.

examples.title: Check expected type
examples.explanation: Parsing and checking type/shape is part of handling incoming data.

examples.title: Trace a boundary
examples.explanation: Mapping data flow reveals where controls belong.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Draw a data flow for a profile form from user input through browser, server, and storage. Mark each trust boundary and write what must be checked at each point.
steps: Draw a data flow for a profile form from user input through browser, server, and storage. Mark each trust boundary and write what must be checked at each point.
Identify the relevant assets, inputs, or permissions.
Choose a control and explain why it applies.
Check edge cases and failure behavior.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: For a signup or feedback feature, create a data-flow diagram with at least four components. Identify untrusted sources and explain which checks must happen on server.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
For a signup or feedback feature, create a data-flow diagram with at least four components. Identify untrusted sources and explain which checks must happen on server.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.

hints: List every component that receives data from outside itself.
A browser can be modified by the user.
Validate shape, type, size, and allowed values.
Enforce security-sensitive rules at the trusted backend.

options: Automatically trusted if formatted as JSON
Trusted when sent by a browser

questions.prompt: Why are browser-only checks insufficient for security?
options: Users can modify client behavior and requests
questions.answer: Users can modify client behavior and requests

questions.answer: User to browser to API to storage

questions.prompt: What should backend input checks consider?

Only whether a field is visible
questions.answer: Type, shape, size, allowed values, and relevant permissions
questions.explanation: Checks should match the operation and trust boundary.
